advances:
Proves exact infeasibility of the entire fixed scalar calibration, including
both branches of the declared support-depth complement.  The contradiction
already occurs between the two endpoint polygons, their four coordinate-cap
areas, the left sides of the two genuine lower crossings, and the diagonal
cap of \(Q\).  It uses no triangular-cap hypothesis, vertex order, support-face
type, rationality, or middle-body compatibility.  It closes only this fixed
calibration and makes no claim about the free-parameter phase layer.
author: r102_phase_fixed_complement
proof:
Put
\[
d_x=-\min_{p\in P}x(p),\qquad
d_y=-\min_{p\in P}y(p),
\]
\[
M_x=\max_{p\in P}x(p),\qquad
M_y=\max_{p\in P}y(p).
\tag{9}
\]
Equations (2)--(4) show that each coordinate cap of \(P\) has positive
area strictly smaller than \(|P|\).  Hence
\[
d_x,d_y,M_x,M_y>0.
\tag{10}
\]

Choose \(p_x\in P\) with \(x(p_x)=-d_x\), and set
\[
\lambda_x=\frac{d_x}{d_x+M_x}.
\tag{11}
\]
Convexity gives
\[
p_x+\lambda_x(P-p_x)\subseteq P.
\tag{12}
\]
Every point of this homothetic copy has \(x\)-coordinate at most zero,
so (2)--(3) imply
\[
16s\lambda_x^2\leq\frac{s}{8}.
\tag{13}
\]
If \(M_x\leq10d_x\), then \(\lambda_x\geq1/11\), and (13) would give
\[
\frac{16s}{121}\leq\frac{s}{8},
\]
contrary to \(128>121\).  Therefore
\[
M_x>10d_x.
\tag{14}
\]
The same homothety based at a point minimizing \(y\) gives
\[
M_y>7d_y.
\tag{15}
\]
Indeed, \(M_y\leq7d_y\) would put a copy of area at least
\(16s/8^2=s/4\) inside the \(y\)-cap of area \(s/5\).

By the definition of \(\delta\), the body \(P\) is contained in
\(\{x+y\leq\delta\}\).  At a point maximizing \(x\), one has
\(y\geq-d_y\), while at a point maximizing \(y\), one has
\(x\geq-d_x\).  Thus
\[
M_x\leq\delta+d_y,\qquad M_y\leq\delta+d_x.
\tag{16}
\]
Equations (14)--(16) yield
\[
\delta>10d_x-d_y,\qquad
\delta>7d_y-d_x.
\tag{17}
\]
Taking respectively \(8/19\) and \(11/19\) of these two strict
inequalities gives
\[
\delta>\frac{69}{19}(d_x+d_y)>3(d_x+d_y)>0.
\tag{18}
\]
In particular, the second branch
\(\delta\geq d_x+d_y\) of the registered support-depth union is forced
by the two \(P\)-cap areas alone; the support face of \(P\) need not be
classified.

We next use the full left-crossing inequalities, not merely their
derivatives at zero.  Put
\[
D_X=-\min_{q\in Q}X(q),\qquad
D_Y=-\min_{q\in Q}Y(q).
\tag{19}
\]
The proper positive-area caps in (3)--(4) imply \(D_X,D_Y>0\).
Substitute \(r=-d_x<0\) in the first inequality of (6).  The set
\(P\cap\{x\leq-d_x\}\) is contained in a supporting line and has
planar area zero.  Hence
\[
|Q\cap\{X\leq d_x\}|\geq\frac{s}{4}.
\tag{20}
\]
After subtracting the \(Q\)-cap in (3), whose cutting line is planar
null, (20) gives
\[
|Q\cap\{0<X\leq d_x\}|\geq\frac{s}{8}.
\tag{21}
\]

Let \(\ell_X(t)\) be the length of the vertical section
\(Q\cap\{X=t\}\).  On the projection interval of \(Q\), the function
\(\ell_X\) is nonnegative and concave: for any two sections, convexity
of \(Q\) contains the corresponding Minkowski interpolation of their
intervals, whose length is the same interpolation of the two lengths.
Since the cap in (3) is proper, zero is in the interior of this
projection interval and \(\ell_X(0)>0\).  Cavalieri's formula and
concavity on \([-D_X,0]\) give
\[
\frac{s}{8}
=\int_{-D_X}^{0}\ell_X(t)\,dt
\geq\frac{D_X}{2}\bigl(\ell_X(-D_X)+\ell_X(0)\bigr)
\geq\frac{D_X\ell_X(0)}{2}.
\tag{22}
\]
For every positive \(t\) in the projection interval, monotonicity of
secant slopes of a concave function gives
\[
\frac{\ell_X(t)-\ell_X(0)}{t}
\leq
\frac{\ell_X(0)-\ell_X(-D_X)}{D_X}
\leq\frac{\ell_X(0)}{D_X}.
\tag{23}
\]
Writing \(A_X=s/8\), equations (22)--(23) therefore imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
|Q\cap\{0<X\leq d_x\}|
&\leq
\ell_X(0)\left(d_x+\frac{d_x^2}{2D_X}\right)\\
&\leq
A_X\left(
\frac{2d_x}{D_X}+\frac{d_x^2}{D_X^2}
\right).
\end{aligned}
\tag{24}
\]
If the positive \(X\)-support of \(Q\) occurs before \(d_x\), the left
side is integrated only to that support; enlarging the upper
integration bound to \(d_x\) in (24) still gives the displayed upper
bound.

Combining (21) and (24), and cancelling \(A_X>0\), yields
\[
1\leq
\frac{2d_x}{D_X}+\frac{d_x^2}{D_X^2}.
\tag{25}
\]
If \(D_X\geq3d_x\), the right side of (25) is at most
\(2/3+1/9=7/9\), a contradiction.  Thus
\[
D_X<3d_x.
\tag{26}
\]

The identical argument in the \(Y\)-coordinate starts from
\(r=-d_y\) in (6), uses the common cap area \(s/5\), and gives
\[
D_Y<3d_y.
\tag{27}
\]
Equations (18), (26), and (27) imply
\[
D_X+D_Y<3(d_x+d_y)<\delta.
\tag{28}
\]
Every \(q\in Q\) consequently satisfies
\[
X(q)+Y(q)\geq-D_X-D_Y>-\delta>-2-\delta.
\tag{29}
\]
Thus all of \(Q\) lies in the halfplane in (7), proving (7) and
contradicting (8).  This contradiction precedes every support-face,
middle-cap, and compatibility condition, so it covers both branches
and every boundary type stated in the registered fixed-calibration
subgoal.
statement:
Let \(s>0\).  Let \(P,Q\subset\mathbb R^2\) be compact
two-dimensional convex bodies, using coordinates \((x,y)\) on \(P\) and
\((X,Y)\) on \(Q\).  Put
\[
\delta=\max_{p\in P}(x(p)+y(p)).
\tag{1}
\]
Assume
\[
|P|=16s,\qquad |Q|=s,
\tag{2}
\]
\[
|P\cap\{x\leq0\}|=|Q\cap\{X\leq0\}|=\frac{s}{8},
\tag{3}
\]
\[
|P\cap\{y\leq0\}|=|Q\cap\{Y\leq0\}|=\frac{s}{5}.
\tag{4}
\]
Define
\[
G_x(r)=|P\cap\{x\leq r\}|+|Q\cap\{X\leq-r\}|,
\]
\[
G_y(r)=|P\cap\{y\leq r\}|+|Q\cap\{Y\leq-r\}|.
\tag{5}
\]
Suppose the left sides of the two exact lower crossings hold:
\[
G_x(r)\geq\frac{s}{4},\qquad
G_y(r)\geq\frac{2s}{5}\qquad(r<0).
\tag{6}
\]
Then
\[
\left|Q\cap\{X+Y\geq-2-\delta\}\right|=s.
\tag{7}
\]
In particular, (2)--(6) are incompatible with
\[
\left|Q\cap\{X+Y\geq-2-\delta\}\right|=\frac{3s}{4}.
\tag{8}
\]
Consequently no rational convex polygons \(P,Q,R\) realize the fixed
calibration in the registered subgoal, regardless of which branch of its
displayed support-depth union holds.
